instr:
# jjui-regen

Working with a recent build of this keyboard-driven terminal front end for a version control system, I hit a scatter of misbehaviour that does not seem to share one cause. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Below is everything I could reproduce, written as what I did and what came back.

Moving a highlight around and acting on whatever it sits on. In the panel that keeps previously issued instructions beside their output, with six entries recorded, the highlight starts on the newest but each press in either direction lands somewhere other than the neighbouring entry; and an entry whose output spans several lines, while it is the highlighted one, is missing from what gets drawn, neither its heading line nor any of its body appearing. Asking to remove the highlighted entry there does nothing at all: it stays in the visible list, it stays in the record behind the list, and the tally of live messages does not drop. Recall in the little field at the bottom is dead as well: with the as-you-type completion hint switched off, the key that opens the prompt for running an external instruction does focus the field, but pressing up leaves it empty instead of bringing back something I ran earlier, and pressing down afterwards yields the same text again rather than a neighbouring entry. And in the list of labels that can be moved onto the current change, pressing the filter key twice highlights the nearby candidate on the first press as it always did,
